interpretation: exploratory; no new blind test or general effectiveness claim

checks.evidence: Four-point means and all station metrics are both retained; 432-day ATU5 improves while the four-point forecast mean worsens. This alone is not a Simpson reversal.
No inference from the four-point mean to each station, a new section or another landslide; simultaneous improvement is checked per station and fold.
One pre-existing case and previously inspected windows are reused; no population correlation or representative sampling claim.
No causal adjustment or treatment-effect regression is performed. Forcing and internal states are model inputs, not causal identification.
No warning classification, event probability, sensitivity or prevalence estimate is reported.
The increment hypothesis follows unfavorable v1.2 diagnostics. Matched C0 results are retained; the repeated historical windows are not a new independent validation.
All four scheduled fitting chains, sixteen stages and twelve evaluated trajectories are retained, including budget and xtol stops; no failed candidates or retries were omitted.
All points, both fixed folds, both prescribed starts and the unselected candidates are retained. No p-values, significance claims or selective positive reporting.

The 30-day window, weight 1, normalization, budgets and training-only selectors were committed before optimization. v1.1/v1.2 negative findings remain; no retrospective weight, stage or forecast-based selection.
The fixed algorithm comparison describes error changes under this implementation and budget. Internal component changes do not establish the true physical cause of landslide motion.
Predictions use prior fitted parameters and observed forcing without future displacement feedback. This temporal data boundary is verified, but does not establish causal direction in nature.

additional_optimization_limit: For 612 days, old C0 B has recalculated J1=32.444117, lower than the best fresh C1 J1=41.801142. No final chain meets gtol. This is a bounded optimization outcome, not proof that all increment objectives are ineffective.
